correctness.rationale: The recursive pruning operation is proved by structural induction and all source/output incidences are completely reproduced in two independently structured Python verifiers. For every size 1 through 6, exact rational primal and dual witnesses satisfy their constraints and have equal objective, while the explicit codebooks have pairwise disjoint deletion shadows. Weak duality and the floor bound prove the stated exact integer maxima. Replayed checks return VERIFY_OK and ALTERNATE_OK; no claim at larger sizes.

evidence: The channel can be recast as ordered plane full binary tree shapes with one leaf and parent suppressed, or as a set-packing problem on the resulting tree-shape shadows.
Matched Dyck parenthesis deletion removes an arbitrary enclosing pair, including pairs whose two child subtrees are nontrivial; it is not the one-terminal-leaf-pruning shadow.
A single-bit Dyck-word deletion does not preserve the binary-tree shape grammar and is another channel.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The same tree can be represented by parenthesizations, Dyck encodings, or explicit ordered-pair shapes; these are only equivalent after the deletion transformation itself is preserved. Generic balanced-word deletions have different output sets, so their results cannot imply exact optima for the defined channel. Searches for shape and parenthesization language did not find a matching capacity classification.

value.rationale: Recovering unlabelled ordered tree shapes from one unknown terminal-leaf pruning is a natural error-control problem for tree-structured representations. The complete finite six-length exact capacity and first strict fractional-packing gap identify a motivated structural limit of the standard output-shadow relaxation, with explicit independently checkable benchmark artifacts. The result is not merely a counting exercise and does not assert a general capacity theorem.
